features.name: Editing, preview and hot-exit recovery
acceptance: Open, preview, pin, split, edit and save files
External save conflicts never overwrite silently
Dirty content survives window restart
Text, image and Markdown preview have safe fallbacks

results: pnpm check passed in full on 2026-07-23: 33 frontend test files, 650 cases, 2283 frontend modules, 2118 bundle sources, 203 recorded migration-debt files and Rust 293/293.
All Browser E2E scenarios passed 22/22 (19 carried over from S1-S5 plus 3 new S7 scenarios: editor-group split, PNG binary-fallback placeholder, Markdown plain-text fallback).

Each S1-S5 slice additionally passed a focused repeat (--repeat-each=3, --retries=0) of its own new scenario(s) before the full-suite run; S7's three new scenarios likewise passed --repeat-each=3 --retries=0 (9/9) before the full-suite run.
nativeScenarios: F030 registered no new real-desktop scenarios of its own in this slice; the real Tauri/WKWebView edit-and-save chain (open via the system folder picker, create/edit/save an exact-byte file, verify on disk) was already established during the F020 single-root desktop acceptance and is the native evidence this feature continues to rely on.

F030's own desktop matrix (kill-9 restart recovery, real CloseRequested close handshake, on-disk backup directory audit) is registered as E2E-003 in docs/e2e-handover.md and handed over to Codex for native execution; it has not yet been executed.
platformGaps: E2E-003 in docs/e2e-handover.md (real hot-exit restart recovery, external-conflict Cmd+S save, and orphan-decoration desktop matrix) is handed over to Codex and not yet executed.

The real Rust WindowEvent::CloseRequested close handshake (veto until the last throttled backup is confirmed flushed, then allow close) is not implemented; PlainWorkingCopyBackupTracker.onFinalBeforeShutdown always returns false, so a normal window close may lose the most recent throttled backup write. This is declared as a known-current-state, not-a-regression condition in E2E-003 and tracked as a follow-up item in docs/e2e-handover.md.

S2's externally-deleted-open-file DELETED detection uses a bounded per-root LRU (256 entries) of resources seen through plainReadFile as an approximation of "currently open files", not a precise open-editor/working-copy reference count; root revocation does not proactively clear this LRU, it only shrinks lazily as new reads evict old entries (harmless because the revoked root stops receiving wakes), so the approximation can lazily retain entries past root removal.

The two new S5 frontend files (plain-workspace-backup-service.ts, plain-workspace-backup-tracker.ts) reuse and minimally extend existing Harness closed-set checks (MIDDLE_SERVICE_DESCRIPTORS, ALLOWED_MONACO_APP_IMPORTS, isAllowedBridgeIdentifier) rather than adding a dedicated AST hostile-mutation suite of the density used by earlier F020 slices; only the real source passing the existing checks was used as positive evidence.
Windows and Linux native packaging remains F120.
Zeroing the monaco-vscode-api bundle migration debt remains F110.

acceptanceResults.acceptance: Open, preview, pin, split, edit and save files
acceptanceResults.result: Open/edit/save are covered by the existing F020 versioned read/write chain and the S3/S5 Browser E2E for dirty tracking and save; preview and pin are covered by the S1 Browser E2E (single-click preview replaces the previous preview tab, double-click or edited content promotes it to pinned). Splitting an editor into multiple groups is now covered by the S7 Browser E2E ('splits an editor into two groups that stay in sync while editing...'): the real Ctrl/Cmd+\ `workbench.action.splitEditor` keybinding produces a second `.editor-group-container` (the real `active`/`inactive` DOM markers `EditorGroupView#setActive` toggles), both groups show a tab for the same resource, editing either side's own Monaco widget updates the other instantly and dirties both tabs together (same shared working copy), a single Ctrl/Cmd+S clears both, and closing the split side's sole tab auto-removes the now-empty group (default closeEmptyGroups) back to one group with the saved content intact. This is still unmodified, inherited default Workbench behavior that F030 did not patch or instrument, but it is no longer an unverified gap.

acceptanceResults.acceptance: External save conflicts never overwrite silently
acceptanceResults.result: The S3 Browser E2E ('shows a Reload/Save As/Details save-conflict notification...') verifies that an external write racing a save surfaces the Plain FILE_MODIFIED_SINCE conflict notification with only Reload/Save As/Details actions (no Retry/Overwrite), leaves the model dirty and the on-disk file untouched, and restores clean state on Reload.

The S5 Browser E2E ('restores an unsaved edit as a dirty editor after a simulated hot-exit reload...') verifies an unsaved edit is backed up, survives a simulated page reload against the persisted browser-mock backup store, and is restored as a dirty editor with the unsaved content on reopening the same workspace, then stops being restored once saved. This is a simulated reload of the mock persistence layer, not a real OS process kill/relaunch against the Rust backup store; the real kill-9-and-relaunch desktop variant is registered as E2E-003 and not yet executed.

acceptanceResults.acceptance: Text, image and Markdown preview have safe fallbacks
acceptanceResults.result: Text editing/preview is exercised throughout every F020/F030 Browser E2E via Monaco. Image and Markdown safe fallbacks are now covered by two new S7 Browser E2E scenarios against a real binary fixture (a genuine 68-byte, CRC-verified PNG whose actual 0x00 bytes trip the real detectEncodingFromBuffer zero-byte scan, not a name/extension special case) and a real plain-text Markdown fixture: opening the PNG shows the real, unmodified upstream BinaryFileEditor placeholder (.monaco-editor-pane-placeholder, the exact upstream 'The file is not displayed in the text editor because it is either binary or uses an unsupported text encoding.' label and its 'Open Anyway' action) with no crash and no .monaco-editor underneath it; opening the Markdown file opens a normal Monaco text editor with a real absence check for any .webview surface and for a 'Markdown: Open Preview' palette command - genuine because Plain bundles no markdown-language-features/media-preview extension and no webview-service-override at all (confirmed against package.json/pnpm-lock.yaml) - and edits save normally through the same write path as every other file. Both paths remain unmodified, inherited default Workbench behavior that F030 did not patch or instrument, but they are no longer an unverified gap.
